articles.title: Schumer, Dems are quietly betting big on one sleeper race in the Deep South
articles.summary: National Democrats reserved $1.2 million in Mississippi ads for Scott Colom as they target Cindy Hyde-Smith's Senate seat in a GOP stronghold.
articles.body: National Democrats are getting aggressive in the homestretch of this election cycle, sending money and party figureheads to a state that, for decades, has been out of reach. Mississippi has been a Republican stronghold for the GOP in the Senate since the 1980s, but in a political environment that is proving tough for incumbents of the party in power, Democrats appear to smell blood in the water. But Republicans aren’t buying the last-minute play in the Deep South, arguing that it’s a reach, at best, to make the race competitive. DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS "Largely, I think they’re just throwing s--- at the wall at this point," a GOP political operative told Fox News Digital. The Senate Majority PAC, a political action committee with close ties to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., reserved $1.2 million in advertising in the state to boost Scott Colom, a district attorney mounting a bid against Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. And major figures in the Democratic Party, like former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, have also made the trip or are set to appear in the state — Buttigieg is scheduled to hold a rally on Mississippi’s Gulf Coast on Tuesday. Jake Monssen, Hyde-Smith’s campaign manager, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "This is simply Washington insiders making a last-ditch effort to give life to Scott Colom's failing campaign." "Scott is bankrolled by the radical left because he is in lockstep with their agenda," Monssen said. "He supports tax increases, open borders, taxpayer benefits for illegal immigrants, and sex change surgeries for minors." Like in other races across the Senate map, Colom has a fight with history to contend with. Mississippi has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982, and the Magnolia State has consistently supported President Donald Trump. TRUMP-BACKED SENATOR ADMITS GOP FACES NIGHTMARE SCENARIO IN STATE REPUBLICANS HAVEN'T LOST IN 90 YEARS But Colom believes that the ground operation he’s developed while national Democrats stayed away from the state is what would put him over the top against Hyde-Smith, not the last-minute support. "It could be enough," Colom told Fox News Digital. "I mean, the thing is, the people of Mississippi built this campaign." Colom went on the offensive against Hyde-Smith, arguing that she "refuses to debate, she doesn’t campaign." "Because of that, I was able to build momentum on the ground, which means now that it's getting attention, now that it's getting resources, I'm able to take advantage of it in a way that other candidates couldn't," he said. Republicans aren’t resting on their laurels in the state, however. The Senate Leadership Fund, a political action committee closely aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., teed up a seven-figure ad buy there in response to Democrats’ spending. And Trump appeared in Corinth, Mississippi, on Monday to rally for Hyde-Smith. He made a similar pitch to voters that he’s done at every rally stop this midterm cycle: pretend he’s on the ballot. "In this election, if you would, I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot," Trump said. "And the reason is that when I'm on the ballot, exactly 49% more people show up." Jonathan Klingler, a professor of political science at the University of Mississippi, told Fox News Digital that the increased spending and national attention to a once-sleepy race have generated the "talking point of Mississippi as evidence for momentum and building a Democratic wave." THUNE MAKES BOLD PREDICTION ABOUT REPUBLICANS' SENATE CHANCES AS GOP PULLS MILLIONS FROM KEY RACES "So at least I'm not — I can't say whether that's the intent of the funding here or visits, but that is the effect," he said. There are also voter demographics that both Hyde-Smith and Colom have to contend with. Mississippi has the highest share of Black voters in the country at nearly 40% of the electorate. In order for Colom and "Democrats to be successful, they simply have to peel off a larger share of White voters," Klingler said. There’s another storyline underneath the headlines of this race, too. Hyde-Smith and Colom have a history dating back to the Biden administration, when the lawmaker blocked his nomination to serve as a district court judge in Mississippi. "Instead of saving himself the embarrassment of being denied a job twice by Hyde-Smith, Colom is running a campaign backed by Chuck Schumer, funded by George Soros, and built on pro-transgender and other far-left policies," National Republican Senatorial Committee spokeswoman Bernadette Breslin told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That’s not Colom’s motivating factor, however. He had just left Trump's northeast Mississippi rally where he spoke to voters about their main concerns, "everybody I talked to, gas prices, grocery prices," and tariffs, he said. But Colom said his personal dispute with Hyde-Smith was not his primary motivation. "I'll tell you, as a Christian, I forgive her for that. That's not a motivating factor for me," Colom said. "I mean, as a district attorney, I have to prosecute cases where people lost their loved ones to gun violence. So, you know, and I’ve seen them forgive that person." "So that's not the motivating factor," he continued. "For me, it's really the betrayal of the America First movement, right? Like she was supposed to help President Trump get lower grocery prices. Well, she betrayed us. We're not getting lower grocery prices."

articles.title: Republican attack ads mocking Troy Jackson’s relationship roil Maine Senate race against Susan Collins
articles.summary: Maine’s battleground Senate race is being roiled by a late burst of Republican ads mocking Democratic nominee Troy Jackson over his relationship with his lon...
articles.body:
Maine's battleground Senate race is being roiled by a late burst of Republican ads mocking Democratic nominee Troy Jackson over his relationship with his longtime partner, whom Sen. Susan Collins and GOP allies have said is his second cousin.

Collins has distanced herself from one radio ad from the Senate Leadership Fund, the top Republican super PAC in Senate races. "If he'll screw his own family, he'll screw yours, too," says the ad, styled as a song about Jackson.

"Senator Collins believes there have been far too many personal attacks in this campaign," Collins campaign spokeswoman Blake Kernen said in a statement. "She called for this ad to be taken down the day it went up."

But Jackson's allies believe Collins implicitly approved scrutiny of his relationship with Lana Pelletier during a September interview.

When asked by Politico's Jonathan Martin whether Jackson's "personal life and the mother of his children" were "relevant" to the race, Collins replied, "Well, I'm not going to bring up the fact that the mother of his two children is his second cousin."

"She's the one who unleashed this," said Rebecca Millett, a former state senator who helped lead a "Women for Troy" news conference after the radio ad's release. "It's the typical her: Bait and run. And then, 'Oh, no, this is terrible.'"

The ad's line of attack has been noteworthy in a state whose politics is known to be relatively civil, amid a race against a battle-tested incumbent whom Democrats almost certainly need to defeat to win Senate control. Jackson and Collins, both from northern Aroostook County, have traded allegations of corruption and ineffectiveness in public office.

Their tension was encapsulated by a recent debate in which Collins said a protester in the crowd was one of Jackson's supporters and he responded with a curt, "Oh, shut up."

Pelletier is a social worker from Allagash who has been in a relationship with Jackson for nearly 40 years. They are not married, but Pelletier describes him as the father of their two children and a grandfather to a recent newborn. The Jackson campaign has not responded to inquiries about whether Pelletier and Jackson are second cousins.

"I have never seen anything like that in Maine politics," Mark Brewer, a political science professor at the University of Maine, said of the radio ad. "That does definitely represent something different."

Jackson's campaign said Collins' call for the ad's removal rings hollow.

"Susan Collins herself spread these disgusting personal attacks on Troy's family," campaign spokesperson Dan Gottlieb said in a statement. "Now she wants Mainers to believe she's above the very attacks she helped spread."

The Senate Leadership Fund did not respond to a request for comment. But it has since launched a different radio ad in the race that more obliquely references the relationship, alluding to a report that Jackson in 2022 helped get a cell tower built on land owned by Pelletier's parents.

SLF has also released a TV ad in the state that brands Jackson a "creep" and suggests it's partly because he "fathered two kids with his cousin."

The chorus of attacks grew loud enough that Pelletier broke her silence in a recent opinion column for the Bangor Daily News. She wrote that she "never imagined U.S. Sen. Susan Collins and her allies would stoop this low."

"Our children have been dragged into this campaign," she said. "Our relationship has been mocked. Our family has been talked about as though there is something shameful about who we are or where we come from. There isn't."

Chris Lydon, the chairman of the Republican Party in Aroostook County, acknowledged family is a sensitive matter for some voters. He questioned whether Jackson's relationship with Pelletier is "the primary thing to judge someone on" but suggested it was worth mentioning.

"I think people do have a right to know," Lydon said.

The race has been consistently tight, with polls showing no clear leader. The candidates are especially fighting over women voters, a voting bloc that Collins narrowly won in her last reelection campaign, according to exit polls.

Collins and Jackson went through a gantlet of four debates in 10 days earlier this month, producing a number of memorable moments displaying how aggravated they have become with one another.

Besides the "shut up" moment, there was an exchange at another debate in which Jackson accused Collins and her husband of profiting off the war in Iran. Collins called the allegation "outrageous" and demanded that Jackson apologize; he did not.

Collins and her allies say that such references to her husband, whose consulting work is targeted in multiple Democratic ads, show that Jackson also bears responsibility for injecting family into the campaign.

Kernen, the Collins spokesperson, argued that unlike the incumbent, Jackson has not distanced himself from attacks involving Susan Collins and her husband.

It's all testing Collins' longtime efforts to campaign as a bipartisan workhorse who eschews the rancor of national politics. The latest drama played out last week as she was campaigning with former West Virginia Sen. Joe Manchin, a Democrat-turned-independent who, like her, has called for more decorum in politics.

The radio ad "goes against her brand, and I can't ever imagine a scenario where Collins herself would release an ad like that," Brewer, the political science professor, said.

Still, Collins and her allies have bombarded Jackson with ads for months depicting him as ill-tempered and erratic. And on Friday, Collins' campaign and the National Republican Senatorial Committee launched a TV ad attacking Jackson over his "shut up" comment, saying "that's how Troy deals with women."

"Troy Jackson is a bully, but Susan is always working for Maine," a narrator concludes in the spot.

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com

articles.title: Armed state Senate hopeful triggers police manhunt near grade school as alarming tweets go viral
articles.summary: Jonathan Miller posted cryptic messages on X during an armed standoff with Cary police near Resurrection Lutheran School on Monday morning..
articles.body: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255). Police arrested a Libertarian North Carolina state Senate candidate Monday after an hours-long armed standoff near a private school, ending a tense confrontation that unfolded as the candidate posted threatening messages on social media. Jonathan Miller, a Libertarian challenging a Democratic incumbent for a North Carolina state Senate seat, raised widespread concern Monday when he began making cryptic and viral posts on X suggesting that he was in the process of an armed pursuit with law enforcement. "The whole police department is chasing me with guns drawn. This should be fun," he wrote around 9:38 a.m. "I've got six shots and the high ground. I hope they don't find me, but if they do it's going to be a hell of a show." LIBERTARIAN TECH MOGUL TO HIT DSA WITH AN EIGHT-FIGURE SPENDING NUKE A number of individuals pleaded with Miller to lay down his arms and surrender, including 2024 Libertarian presidential nominee Chase Oliver. Responding to Oliver at 10:04 a.m., Miller claimed that he had "reached the tree line," indicating that he was attempting to hide in the woods. Responding to another user offering to send him money, Miller claimed that he "gave away all [his] money to charity" and that he didn’t "want or need yours." Police said they received calls from concerned members of the public after Miller posted messages Sunday night suggesting he was considering suicide. Officers attempted to check on his welfare Monday morning, and during a subsequent encounter, Miller was carrying a firearm. Police said he fled after being ordered not to touch the weapon. 'MODERATE' AG'S OFFICE TURNED TO GROUPS THAT SPENT YEARS SUING PRISONS FOR RECRUITING HELP, EMAILS REVEAL WRAL, a local NBC affiliate, managed to get Miller on the phone during his standoff with the police, where he gave his side of the story. "Last night I was pretty depressed and suicidal, and I sort of put a suicide note on X, and it has gone quite viral," he told WRAL during one such call. "Actually, millions of people have seen it. I usually get about 50 views on my post, but this one has gone super viral on me. I spent all night crying, and angry and upset, and depressed, and all the emotions. And this morning I was tired, but I had things I needed to do. And I didn't kill myself. "So I got up and made coffee," Miller continued, "and I had two sips of coffee, and I went outside to have a cigarette, and while I was having a cigarette, a police officer approached me, knew my name, saw that I had a holstered revolver on my hip, so he drew his weapon and told me to keep my hands away from mine. I told him I was going to refuse that order, and I backed away slowly until I was far enough away from him to turn and run, and then I turned and ran into the woods." DOJ OPENS NEW PATHWAY TO RESTORE FEDERAL GUN RIGHTS FOR CERTAIN BARRED INDIVIDUALS Cary Police Chief Terry Sult stated that Miller had a warrant for being a felon in possession of a firearm. Police expressed fear that the public could be in harm's way as a result of the standoff, urging pedestrians and motorists to avoid the surrounding area. The armed confrontation unfolded near Resurrection Lutheran School, a private K-8 school that was placed under a code yellow lockdown for part of Monday as police searched for Miller, according to local reports. "They had some hostage negotiator type dude call me. While I was distracted talking with him on the phone they were moving in around me. Luckily I spotted one of them and took off," Miller posted to X around 1:46 p.m. Around 3 p.m., law enforcement officers closed in on Miller and arrested him without incident. He has been charged with communicating threats, resisting a public officer, going armed to the terror of the people and possession of a firearm by a felon. No shots were fired during the confrontation, according to police. The Libertarian Party of North Carolina told the New York Post that it was "aware of the situation," thanking law enforcement for "pursuing a solution without involving violence." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Miller is running for office on a relatively standard Libertarian platform of weakening legal protections for police, repealing drug laws and reducing economic regulations.

articles.title: House report says NYC prosecutors tailored plea deals to shield illegal immigrants from deportation
articles.summary: House Judiciary Committee claims New York City district attorneys trained prosecutors to craft immigration-safe plea deals for noncitizen defendants.
articles.body: New York City prosecutors from all five boroughs have given "preferential treatment" to noncitizens who commit crimes, all to help them avoid deportation, according to a report from the GOP-led House Judiciary Committee. The committee, chaired by Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, said nonpublic documents obtained through its oversight work revealed new details about the extent to which the city's district attorney's offices sought to limit the immigration consequences of criminal prosecutions. Some of the report's most serious allegations came against Bronx District Attorney Darcel Clark. The report claims she "trains prosecutors in her office to conceal certain facts" from defendants' conviction records and pursue charges that would not trigger deportation. Internal materials from the Bronx DA's office explicitly instruct prosecutors to leave references to firearms out of conviction records to maintain "immigration-conscious plea bargaining," according to the report. SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP In cases of domestic violence or crimes against children — offenses that are often deportable under the Immigration and Nationality Act — Bronx prosecutors were told to leave out defendants' relationships with their alleged victims and pursue charges that did not specify the ages of child victims. Clark, who has been the Bronx DA since 2016, was also accused of encouraging prosecutors to charge foreign nationals with "nonexistent, legally impossible" crimes to skirt deportation. The report's authors offered the example of Clark's staff getting someone to plead guilty to "attempted reckless assault," a crime they described as legally impossible because someone cannot intend to act recklessly. A plea to such a crime, they said, could allow a noncitizen defendant to stay in the country indefinitely. New York courts nevertheless allow defendants to plead guilty to such hypothetical offenses as part of negotiated plea deals. The Court of Appeals, the state's highest court, upheld the legal concept this year. DENVER, BOULDER IGNORED ICE DETAINERS FOR MIGRANTS WITH CHILD ABUSE, ASSAULT ARRESTS, HOUSE GOP REPORT REVEALS The practice is not limited to the Bronx. State data obtained by the Immigrant Defense Project showed 289 convictions for attempted reckless assault across New York City from 2015 through 2025, including 50 in the Bronx. The House Judiciary Committee also pointed to similar practices within the Queens DA's office, led by Melinda Katz since 2020. It cited a May 2026 email from a Queens prosecutor informing an NYPD detective that the DA's office had "basically made a [plea] deal which is ‘immigration safe’ while still having [the defendant] plea to multiple crimes and do some jail time." Queens prosecutors were also instructed to "exercise extreme caution" when resolving cases involving noncitizens and to consult the office's immigration specialist when considering plea deals for them, the report said. WATCH: DEM DEMANDS 'ONE CASE' WHERE SANCTUARY CITIES DIDN'T TURN OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS; DHS PROVIDES LIST Over in the Manhattan office, the report said DA Alvin Bragg issued a memo in 2022 telling prosecutors to "seek dispositions that avoid immigration consequences for all misdemeanors, and all felonies" where prosecutors generally did not expect defendants to receive jail time. Bragg's office responded to the committee by describing its January 2022 policy as "outdated," adding that it had updated it to give prosecutors discretion on individual cases. The DA's offices in Brooklyn and Staten Island were alleged to have used comparable tactics when dealing with noncitizen defendants, according to the report. In a statement to Fox News Digital, the Staten Island DA's office called the House Judiciary Committee's report "flagrantly false and patently political." "[The Richmond County District Attorney's Office] has and will continue to ask ICE to let us prosecute and convict criminals before they deport them because Congress has failed to secure our borders. That is the only way to guarantee our victims justice and to keep our communities safe. If you believe in law and order, that’s the only way to do the job," the office said. DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION The four other offices referenced in the report did not immediately respond to a Fox News Digital request for comment. The mayor's office also did not immediately respond. Citywide sanctuary policies led the NYPD to decline 20,255 immigration detainers between July 2018 and June 2026, the report said. Detainers are federal requests asking local authorities to hold certain noncitizens briefly so Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) can take them into custody. The city's Department of Correction also declined all 2,852 ICE detainers it received during the same period, according to the report. These figures are not necessarily surprising, given that each mayoral administration throughout that period has limited city agencies from cooperating with ICE. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP What stands out, however, is that nearly half of those detainers — almost 10,000 — were lodged between July 2025 and June 2026, an indicator that the second Trump administration has acted far more aggressively in its attempts to scoop up noncitizens arrested by local police than either the Biden administration or the first Trump administration. The House Judiciary Committee's findings come as House Republicans push legislation that would prevent state and local governments from restricting cooperation with federal immigration authorities. In March, the committee advanced the Shut Down Sanctuary Policies Act — a bill that has stalled in the House — and the report said lawmakers would continue investigating sanctuary jurisdictions.

articles.title: Hundreds of staged armed robberies helped thousands pose as crime victims in US immigration scam: DOJ
articles.summary: Parth Nayi organized hundreds of staged armed robberies at Chicago-area businesses to help noncitizens fraudulently apply for U visas in exchange for cash.
articles.body: A "ringleader" has been sentenced and several other suspects charged in Illinois in connection with a widespread conspiracy to defraud the federal immigration system by helping noncitizens seek visa protections reserved for crime victims who assist law enforcement. Parth Nayi of Illinois was sentenced Thursday to two years in federal prison for participating in hundreds of staged armed robberies at small businesses and eateries in and around Chicago and helping "coach" the supposed " victims" through plans to apply for U visas in exchange for cash. "[Nayi] was the main organizer and at the center of almost every single one of the hundreds of staged robberies that were perpetrated. [The] defendant significantly corrupted the federal U-Visa program, designed to provide a benefit to a particularly vulnerable group—foreign nationals who are victims of serious crimes while visiting the United States," Assistant U.S. Attorney Saqib Mohammad Hussain wrote in the case’s sentencing memo. TRUMP ADMIN’S FRAUD CRACKDOWN TARGETS FOREIGNERS ACCUSED OF INFILTRATING US FEDERAL PROGRAMS Thousands of people posing as crime victims paid Nayi to participate in the scheme, prosecutors said. Alleged co-conspirators Bhikhabhai Patel, Nilesh Patel, Ravinaben Patel and Rajnikumar Patel reached out to Nayi to pose as victims of the staged robberies so they could apply for U visas, which were created under a 2000 law meant to protect trafficking victims and "battered immigrant women." Rep. Christopher Smith, R-N.J., lead sponsor of the anti-trafficking legislation that created the U visa, expressed outrage over the alleged abuse of the program. "Anyone who engages in visa fraud or falsifies claims to obtain any government benefit should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law, and if guilty, jailed," Smith told Fox News Digital on Tuesday. "It is especially egregious to abuse a program designed to help victims of human trafficking — often women and children — who are cooperating with police and are working to recover from their extraordinary trauma. We must hold abusive criminals accountable." Prosecutors said Nayi and another suspect, Kewon Young, recruited people to serve as armed "robbers" who at times "struck purported victims to make the staged robbery appear real." Nayi and alleged co-conspirator Kewon Young organized and participated in staged robberies of shops and bodegas. After the "robberies," the purported victims would be coached to submit I-918 supplements to law enforcement so authorities could certify that they had been victims of a violent crime and could seek U visas. An I-918 form would then be submitted to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) seeking protected legal status in the United States. Purported victims paid Nayi as much as $30,000 to take part in the staged robberies, prosecutors said. During one robbery, a store employee was critically injured by a gunshot fired by one of the alleged assailants. ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ILLINOIS TEACHER LINKED TO TREN DE ARAGUA MASS SHOOTING During a July 2023 "robbery" at a Chicago liquor store, one of the alleged assailants accidentally discharged his weapon and "critically" injured an employee, according to CWB Chicago. The perpetrators then fled in a stolen vehicle, according to the outlet. Fox News Digital reached out to Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker for comment. Johnson has repeatedly lambasted federal immigration enforcement, particularly under the Trump administration, likening its actions to an America that appears as if the "Confederacy won" the Civil War. Bhikhabhai Patel allegedly posed as a victim at a Chicago Dunkin' in 2023 before filing a fraudulent U visa application. Ravinaben Patel allegedly posed as a victim at a second Dunkin' and filed a false police report about the incident. The 2024 indictment identified more than a dozen locations used in the scheme, including businesses outside Illinois, such as a Subway in Louisiana and a truck stop in Middle Tennessee. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER The DOJ’s indictment indicates five others besides Nayi have been convicted but does not specify their names. articles.title: Cuban exile-turned-congressman unloads on Dem Senate hopeful over Cuba remarks
articles.summary: Cuban-American Rep. Carlos Gimenez blasted Florida Democrat Angie Nixon over her Cuba remarks after CBS News apologized for mischaracterizing her response.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: A Cuban-American congressman whose family fled Cuba's communist regime slammed Florida Democratic Senate candidate Angie Nixon, accusing her of not going far enough in condemning the island nation's dictatorship. Nixon, the Florida state representative running to unseat Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., pushed back after CBS News initially characterized her remarks during an interview aired Monday as a refusal to call Cuba a dictatorship. "Do you consider that Cuba is a dictatorship?" the interviewer asked Nixon. "That is what people have told me. I have never been to Cuba, and so I will have to take their word for it," Nixon, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), responded. FLORIDA SENATE CANDIDATE ANGIE NIXON CALLS FOR JAILING GOP OPPONENT ASHLEY MOODY In a now deleted tweet, CBS accused Nixon of refusing to answer the question, which Nixon responded to as "a serious failure of editorial reporting." "To claim I declined to answer the question is categorically false. That is not journalism. It is misinformation," Nixon added in her online response. CBS has since re-uploaded the footage on X and apologized for the misleading language. However, Rep. Carlos Gimenez, R-Fla., whose family fled Cuba when he was young, told Fox News Digital that he still believes Nixon refused to acknowledge the island nation's regime. "There is no ambiguity: Cuba is a communist dictatorship that has imprisoned, tortured, and murdered innocent people for decades," the congressman said. "Floridians deserve leaders who stand unequivocally for freedom, not politicians who whitewash the horrors of communism." Cuba has been under communist rule since 1959. RUBIO WARNS CUBA HAS INFILTRATED US WITH SPIES, CALLS COMMUNIST REGIME AN 'ESPIONAGE SUPERPOWER' Ian Vallecillo, a South Florida lawmaker whose family escaped the totalitarian regime in Nicaragua, echoed Gimenez's claim in a statement to Fox News Digital. "This is a perfect example of ideological cognitive dissonance. Acknowledging Cuba’s dictatorship means confronting the failure of a Marxist system she appears sympathetic to," the lawmaker stated. "Cuba is a nearly 70-year experiment in Marxism that has produced economic devastation, repression, and a brutal dictatorship. Yet these are the same people who constantly accuse Trump and Republicans of being dictators, while hesitating to acknowledge actual dictatorships that align with their ideology." Vallecillo accused Nixon of "showing her true colors," who has a biased view of communist regimes since she and her fellow DSA members have spent "their lives defending a failed ideology and therefore cannot recognize that they are on the wrong side of history." RNC WARNS DEMOCRATS FACE 'POLITICAL SUICIDE' AFTER DSA PRAISES FIDEL CASTRO, DEMANDS RUBIO'S PROSECUTION Nixon did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. During her interview, Nixon criticized the decades-long U.S. embargo on Cuba and expressed support for returning to policies implemented under former President Barack Obama, arguing that such an approach could help address the island's widespread blackouts and shortages of medical care. In 2014, Obama began a diplomatic thaw with Cuba, restoring diplomatic relations and easing certain economic and travel restrictions imposed during the Cold War. RUBIO URGES CUBANS TO WORK WITH CIA TO BRING POLITICAL CHANGE TO COMMUNIST-RUN ISLAND The Obama administration also removed Cuba from the State Department's list of state sponsors of terrorism in 2015 and eased restrictions on certain forms of trade with the island nation. Nixon and other DSA members have long argued that the U.S. embargo contributes to the deteriorating living conditions faced by the Cuban people. CUBA’S DICTATORSHIP HAS LONG BEEN A THREAT TO AMERICA. NOW, IT’S FINALLY TEETERING President Donald Trump’s administration has maintained that certain U.S. sanctions target businesses tied to Cuba's military, including Grupo de Administración Empresarial S.A. (GAESA), a conglomerate controlled by the Cuban armed forces. According to reports, GAESA is worth over $14.5 billion and oversees 37% of the country's gross domestic product. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "That's not sanctions on the Cuban people. The Cuban people don't benefit from GAESA," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said.

articles.title: Trump accused of trying to 'force' Senate candidate on voters as GOP feud erupts
articles.summary: Ralph Norman refuses to campaign for Darline Graham, accusing Trump of trying to force his hand-picked Senate candidate on South Carolina voters.
articles.body: A growing intraparty fracture is roiling the South Carolina Senate race as a Republican congressman is accusing President Donald Trump of trying to force his hand-picked candidate on Palmetto State voters. Rep. Ralph Norman, R-S.C., who lost to Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., in a runoff for the Senate GOP nomination earlier this year, told Fox News Digital on Tuesday that he has no plans to help Graham in the final week before Election Day. "The voters in S.C. are not buying the argument that everyone has to ‘settle’ for a candidate that has been propped up by special interest groups and a Republican president spending millions of dollars spreading false narratives about why Darlene [sic] Graham is qualified to be elected to the U.S. Senate for the next six years," Norman told Fox News Digital via text message in all capital letters. He said the general election "is about attempts to ‘force’ a candidate on the voters of S.C. and regardless of the outcome, it didn’t have to be this way as the great people living in South Carolina deserve ‘better!!’" TRUMP ENDORSEMENT BOOSTS SISTER OF LATE LINDSEY GRAHAM TO HISTORIC RUNOFF VICTORY "Elections have consequences," Norman ended the message. It’s a pointed attack at the leader of the Republican Party just a week before voters decide who controls Congress for the final two years of Trump’s presidency. Graham, who was appointed to replace her brother, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., is running a closer-than-expected race in her Republican home state. THE NINE KEY RACES THAT WILL DECIDE WHO CONTROLS THE SENATE, AND WHERE THEY STAND Norman said he would refuse to campaign with or for Graham, no matter who asked him to help. He told Fox News Digital her campaign manager had asked his chief of staff if he would campaign with her, but that Norman refused. That’s despite pressure from fellow House Republicans like Rep. Russell Fry, R-S.C., who told reporters this week, "As somebody who carried the conservative banner as long as he has, he should step into the arena," according to Politico. Like Norman, Fry lost his own bid for the GOP nomination for the late senator’s seat. National Republicans are making the case for Graham, too, arguing that the GOP is united behind her. "At the end of the day, Republicans are unified on beating Annie Andrews," Republican National Committee spokeswoman Emma Hall told Fox News Digital. "Democrats’ socialism has no place in South Carolina, and that’s why President Trump supports Darline Graham." SC DEM SENATE CANDIDATE CLAIMS SHE WILL STAND UP TO HER PARTY AS GRAHAM TIES HER TO 'SOCIALIST DEMOCRATS' Norman’s decision comes after a bitter, whirlwind primary where he ultimately lost to the political novice in August. Since then, Trump has returned to the Palmetto State to support Graham, holding a rally in Clemson, S.C., last week as election forecasters have signaled a more competitive race. The nonpartisan Cook Political Report shifted the contest from "Likely Republican" to "Lean Republican" last week. And Trump isn’t the only one trying to boost her candidacy. The Senate Leadership Fund, a political action committee closely aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., pledged $5 million in ad spending in South Carolina earlier this month. Other big political names in the state are jumping ship from Graham, too. Two former South Carolina governors, Republican David Beasley and Democrat Jim Hodges, are reportedly backing Graham’s opponent, Annie Andrews. TRUMP WON THIS RELIABLY RED STATE BY DOUBLE DIGITS. NOW A DEADLOCKED RACE IS BRINGING HIM BACK Norman’s son, Warren, bucked Graham in an op-ed for FITS News last week. He wrote that he would "not be voting" for the lawmaker and contended that he was leaning toward Andrews. "As of today, I’m leaning her way. It will be the first time in my life I’ve voted for a Democrat in a partisan election," he wrote. "I know the concern many conservatives will have: isn’t a vote against Graham a vote for the liberal agenda? I’ve thought hard about that. Unfortunately, there is no true conservative to vote for in this election." Norman previously told "The Nashional Briefing with Kelly Nash" that he would vote for Graham, but his family would not. When reached for comment on Tuesday, the White House pointed Fox News Digital to Trump’s comments at his South Carolina rally. "You must vote for Darline and Republicans, and just — you're going to be happy," Trump said. "I tell you, you're going to look back years from now. You're going to say it was truly one of the greatest votes you ever made. High-quality person, and she's going to be great." articles.title: Ilhan Omar's radical streamer ally rallies with embattled lawmaker after DC home raid
articles.summary: Hasan Piker defended his alliance with Ilhan Omar after their Minnesota campaign event drew sharp criticism from Amy Klobuchar and other Democrats.
articles.body: Far-left streamer Hasan Piker dodged his controversial past in an exchange with Fox News Digital on Tuesday, hours after teaming up with embattled Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., on the campaign trail to co-host an event in her home state of Minnesota. He also dismissed his disagreements with Democratic Party leaders after he called Republicans "terrorists" and Omar said the GOP is the "pedophile protection party" during the stream on Monday. Omar's decision to embrace Piker on the campaign trail marks a potentially risky political alliance, coming on the back of a high-profile raid on her Washington, D.C., home amid two dueling investigations — one for alleged immigration fraud, which could threaten her political future and citizenship status, and the other for fishy financial disclosure statement discrepancies. The lawmaker's appearance with Piker comes after Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed drew backlash from his own party for campaigning with the controversial Twitch streamer earlier this cycle. HASAN PIKER LASHES OUT AT REPUBLICANS, CALLS THEM 'TERRORISTS' IN EVENT WITH ILHAN OMAR Fox News Digital confronted Piker at the Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport heading out of Minnesota after the Monday livestream. He was pressed on the criticism stemming from Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., and Minnesota gubernatorial candidate Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., after the two condemned Piker’s comments and pushed back on Democrats’ choice to engage with him on the campaign trail. "Well, Angie Craig lost, and I think Klobuchar is going to make for a great governor," Piker told Fox News Digital while walking to security. Klobuchar condemned Piker’s past statements as "reckless and unacceptable," while Craig called his rhetoric "polarizing and dangerous" and directly called out Minnesota Democrats, like Omar and Fateh, for hosting Monday’s event with Piker as a "mistake." When asked if the two Democratic lawmakers in Minnesota were right to call out the rhetoric, Piker wrote off their disagreements as "the beauty of democracy," while also throwing jabs at Fox News. "I know this is probably going to come across as confusing, because you work for Fox News, but we sometimes disagree with our leadership in the Democratic Party," he said. "And sometimes our leadership disagrees with us." "But at the end of the day," he continued, "that's the beauty of democracy." HASAN PIKER ADMITS HE HAS 'DIALED DOWN' HIS OPINIONS AFTER PUBLIC AND DEMOCRATIC BACKLASH The controversy over the Somali-born congresswoman deciding to sit down with Piker with just over one week until the 2026 midterms exposes a divide among Minnesota Democrats — is it justifiable to work with Piker in order to rally his large, young, progressive base to get out and vote despite his heavily condemned commentary? Piker was asked on Tuesday about his previous comments on Jewish people and Israel after prominent Democrats joined Republicans who have called the streamer antisemitic. He suggested that Jewish Americans were inviting violence against themselves over their support for Israel. He has repeatedly stood by his comments against Israel over its ongoing war against Hamas in Gaza. "Anti-Zionism is not antisemitism," Piker told Fox News Digital. "I will always fight against antisemitism and I find all bigotry to be morally repugnant and completely unacceptable. But I also find it a real shame to constantly complain about people who are outspoken on the issue of Israel's genocide." It was after Democrats, including House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., began calling out Piker for his extreme comments that El-Sayed distanced himself after frequently making appearances side-by-side. Another reason why Omar’s choice to engage with Piker has been questioned within the party. Piker refused to comment on one issue though — his past comments claiming America "deserved 9/11." "You made some comments on 9/11, do you still stand by them?" Fox News Digital asked Piker, at which point he ignored the question and walked through the line for security. Both Piker and Omar attacked President Donald Trump during their event Monday night, with the Somali-born lawmaker ripping his "obsession" with Minnesotans. Piker, meanwhile, shamed Democrats for ceding on immigration arguments to Trump's agenda back in 2024. REP ILHAN OMAR'S IMMIGRATION HISTORY FACES NEW SCRUTINY AS FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS SUBPOENA RELATIVES "That's unacceptable. Migrants are not a national security threat. They are our neighbors. They are allies. They work alongside us. They are not the burden, but a benefit. They are what make this country strong, and they're what make it this country great," Piker insisted. "Any Democrat that refuses to recognize that, in my opinion, is un-American," he concluded. Omar is running for reelection and projected for a clear win, despite being under investigation by both Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) and the Department of Justice (DOJ) for immigration fraud and questionable financial filings. The Minnesota Democrat’s name has also come into question following HSI’s raid on her Washington, D.C., home, with a new federal court filing referring to her as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar," as first reported by Fox News Digital. A source told Fox that the language used for her name in the filing was reflective of the evidence compiled in the immigration fraud probe into Omar. articles.title: Is that campaign merch store official? Here's how to tell
articles.summary: Attaxion researchers found 30 fake Texas campaign merchandise stores traced to just two sellers hawking gear for competing Republicans and Democrats.
articles.body: You're scrolling online when you spot a campaign T-shirt supporting your favorite candidate. The website looks professional, the merchandise looks legitimate and the address includes the candidate's name. You might even see the word "official" at the top of the page. So, you assume your purchase supports the campaign. But what if the candidate has nothing to do with that store? With the Nov. 3 midterm elections approaching, new research shared with CyberGuy reveals a troubling discovery in Texas. Researchers at cybersecurity company Attaxion identified 626 unofficial election-related domains, including 30 online merchandise stores presenting themselves as official campaign shops. Attaxion says it could not verify an official campaign connection for any of the 30 stores. Even more surprising, researchers found that nearly all appeared to come from just two sellers offering merchandise for competing Republicans and Democrats. The findings arrive as the FBI warns about election-related scams involving fake merchandise, fraudulent donations and websites designed to steal personal information. And while this investigation focuses on Texas, the warning signs apply to elections and online shopping across the country. Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. DON'T LET FAKE ELECTION WEBSITES FOOL YOU BEFORE 2026 MIDTERMS Researchers uncover 626 unofficial Texas election domains Texas voters are already heading to the polls. Early voting for the Nov. 3 general election began Oct. 19 and continues through Oct. 30. Meanwhile, researchers are finding that candidates' names have become valuable online real estate. Attaxion, a cybersecurity company that helps organizations identify vulnerable websites and other online threats, examined domains connected to the state's U.S. Senate race, governor's race and six competitive congressional districts. The investigation also included websites resembling election offices and voter information pages. Researchers initially identified 704 domains. After excluding 25 official sites and another 53 domains connected to campaigns or election offices, 626 unofficial addresses remained. Of those, 553 had DNS records when checked. That means the domains had some internet configuration, although it does not establish that each hosted an active website. The Senate race accounted for 323 unofficial domains. Another 75 referenced House candidates, while 70 used gubernatorial candidates' names. The remaining domains referenced election offices or general election-related terms. Importantly, an unofficial domain is not automatically a scam. Some may belong to supporters, critics or independent businesses. Others may be registered without hosting an active website. However, the researchers identified a smaller group that deserves closer attention. 30 Texas campaign merchandise stores raise questions Of the 626 unofficial domains, Attaxion identified 30 online stores that presented themselves as official merchandise sellers for Texas political candidates. The stores promoted products associated with Republican U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton and Democratic opponent James Talarico. Others used the names of Republican Gov. Greg Abbott and his Democratic challenger, Gina Hinojosa. Researchers also identified stores featuring congressional candidates. Alexandre François, research contributor at Attaxion, worked on the investigation and shared the findings with CyberGuy. "Two things stood out. The first is how little the politics seem to matter to the people selling," François told CyberGuy. He explained that nearly all the stores appeared to come from the same two sellers, despite promoting candidates from opposing parties. In Texas' 23rd Congressional District, researchers found stores supporting the Republican and Democratic nominees that appeared to share an operator. That raises an obvious question. If a business is selling merchandise for competing candidates, is it really connected to either campaign? According to the investigation, none of the 30 stores could be verified as campaign-operated. Two sellers appear to control nearly all 30 stores Attaxion traced most of the merchandise websites to two seller identities: ShirtGoat and madetoprints. ShirtGoat appeared to operate 12 stores and was likely connected to two more. Meanwhile, madetoprints was associated with another 15. The researchers found that both sellers used similar website templates while swapping out candidates' names and merchandise. Some sites also borrowed slogans that appeared on official campaign products. For example, when Talarico's campaign responded to a political nickname with an "I'm a Talafreako" shirt, similar products appeared in three unofficial stores. "It suggests that the motive is most likely commercial rather than political," François explained. "Someone with a political agenda would be unlikely to sell merchandise for both sides of the same race." Researchers also noticed that several domains were registered on the same day. Some stores reused identical policies with only the candidate's name changed. A few terms-of-service pages even contained apparent chatbot responses left behind during the creation process. That suggests some operators may be creating these stores quickly and repeatedly. However, the researchers could not establish the legal identities of the people controlling all the websites. Why these political merchandise websites look legitimate One of the biggest challenges is how convincing the stores can appear. A website might feature professional product photos and familiar campaign slogans. It may also offer a functional shopping cart with a normal-looking checkout. Those features can create confidence before someone even thinks to check who operates the business. François says that assumption can be risky. "The first thing to know is that appearance is no longer a reliable guide. With AI, anyone can quickly build a polished store with well-written text, so the old signs of poor design and clumsy language rarely apply, and neither does the word ‘official.’" Attaxion found that none of the 30 unofficial stores included the campaign-related "Paid for by" disclosure the researchers expected to see. However, independent businesses selling political merchandise are not automatically required to display campaign finance disclaimers. The missing disclosure is one warning sign, not proof of fraud or a legal violation. The stores also failed to provide a verifiable company identity and business address. Some listed a seller name or customer service email address. However, those details did not establish an official relationship with a candidate. To investigate the websites, Attaxion compared them against verified campaign information from the Federal Election Commission and Texas Ethics Commission. Researchers also examined registration records and revisited the stores on Oct. 20 to check their contact pages, policies and checkout processes. None of those checks established a connection to the campaigns. 119,000 FAKE SHOPS COULD STEAL YOUR CREDIT CARD DETAILS A former election website now promotes an online casino The researchers uncovered another unusual example involving an expired election website. The domain elpasoelections.com sounds like it could belong to an election office in El Paso, Texas. However, it previously served El Paso County in Colorado. That county used the address for election information for years before allowing its registration to lapse in February 2026. A domain buyer acquired the address in May. When researchers examined the website, it displayed an online casino promoting itself to Australian users. The investigation identified a new registrant organization associated with Hong Kong, although that record does not independently establish who operates the casino. François highlighted the discovery as an example of how a once-legitimate web address can change hands. "It is a good reminder that a familiar-looking address does not tell you who holds it today." The example extends well beyond politics. An expired website previously used by a government office, nonprofit or business can eventually lead somewhere completely unrelated. For accurate Texas election information, the state's official website is VoteTexas.gov. For voting information elsewhere in the country, you can start with Vote.gov. FBI warns about election merchandise and donation scams The Texas findings follow an Oct. 15 warning from the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center. The agency warned that criminals exploit political campaigns to target people across the United States. Some scammers impersonate candidates to solicit fraudulent contributions. Others advertise political merchandise that customers never receive. The FBI also warned about fraudulent voter-registration messages that direct people to websites designed to collect personal information. Artificial intelligence can make these schemes harder to recognize. Criminals can generate convincing written messages and realistic voices that appear to come from legitimate organizations. However, there's an important limitation to the Texas investigation. Attaxion did not determine whether customers lost money through the 30 stores. "At this stage we do not know. We did not place test orders, and our research does not include payment records or customer complaints, so we have no evidence either way," François told CyberGuy. The researchers also did not investigate whether the operators promoted their stores through Google ads, social media or political text messages. They did examine observed DNS traffic and found that some unofficial domains had received lookups. However, those records cannot establish how someone discovered a website or whether they completed a purchase. The findings raise concerns about misleading campaign connections without proving that all the stores committed fraud. How to protect yourself from fake campaign websites and online scams These precautions apply to political merchandise stores and fundraising pages nationwide. They can also help you recognize ordinary shopping scams and websites that impersonate trusted organizations. 1. Start with a website you can verify Before buying political merchandise or making a donation, find the candidate's established campaign website. Look for the merchandise or contribution page linked directly from that website. For federal candidates, you can also use the Federal Election Commission's database to verify campaign committees and find their reported information. If you're shopping from an unfamiliar retailer, visit its official website independently rather than following a promotional link. This approach also works when someone claims to represent a bank, charity or government agency. 2. Check the full website address Scammers and unauthorized sellers can register web addresses that closely resemble legitimate ones. Look for misspellings or added words that make an unfamiliar address appear trustworthy. Don't assume a website belongs to an organization simply because the address contains its name or the word "official." You can also use a WHOIS lookup to investigate when a domain was registered. A newly created website deserves closer attention, especially when it claims to represent an established organization. However, domain age alone cannot establish whether a website is legitimate. And remember, HTTPS encryption protects information while it travels between your browser and a website. It does not prove that the site's operator is trustworthy. WHY VERIFIED SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS CAN STILL LEAD YOU INTO A SCAM 3. Verify who receives your money Before contributing to a political campaign, confirm the organization receiving the payment. Federal political committee websites generally must include a disclaimer identifying who paid for the communication. When applicable, the disclosure also identifies the campaign or committee that authorized it. Look for a "Paid for by" statement and compare the information with official campaign records. Many political campaigns use fundraising platforms such as ActBlue or WinRed. Others use different payment systems. The key is reaching the contribution page through the campaign's verified website. Independent businesses may legally sell political merchandise without supporting a campaign. However, they should not mislead you about who receives your money. A missing or suspicious disclosure deserves attention, but a disclaimer alone does not guarantee legitimacy. 4. Investigate unfamiliar sellers before purchasing Take a closer look at any online store you've never used before. Search for the company name along with terms such as "reviews," "complaints" or "scam." Read its return and refund policies. Look for a legitimate way to reach customer support. The Better Business Bureau at bbb.org/ can be another place to check for complaints, although the absence of complaints does not prove a company is trustworthy. If you cannot establish who operates a website, consider buying elsewhere. 5. Be skeptical of unexpected texts and emails A scammer may send a message claiming that your voter registration needs attention. Another might pressure you to contribute immediately or purchase merchandise before an offer disappears. The same tactics appear in fake bank alerts and fraudulent delivery notifications. Avoid clicking payment or account-verification links in unsolicited messages. Instead, open the organization's established website yourself. For election-related messages, check information through Vote.gov or your state election office. Be especially cautious about messages asking for passwords, Social Security numbers or payment details. 6. Use safer payment methods When shopping online, paying with a credit card generally gives you stronger protections if an order never arrives or a charge is incorrect. Avoid unfamiliar sellers that insist on payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or wire transfers. Those methods can make recovering your money difficult. Keep your purchase confirmation and review your statements after paying. Also, check whether a political contribution involves recurring payments before submitting it. The FTC's online shopping guide explains how to research sellers and protect yourself when making purchases. 7. Protect your accounts and personal information A suspicious shopping site may ask you to create an account before checking out. Never reuse a password from your email, banking or other important accounts. Use a password manager to create unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication (2FA) when available. Strong antivirus software can also help detect malicious downloads and block some dangerous websites. However, it cannot verify whether a political merchandise store is actually affiliated with a campaign. Be selective about the information you share, especially when you cannot verify who operates the website. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. What to do if you already paid a suspicious website If you've purchased merchandise or sent money through a questionable website, act promptly when something appears wrong. If you entered sensitive identity information into a suspicious website, visit IdentityTheft.gov for personalized recovery guidance. Kurt's key takeaways What stands out to me about this investigation is that the people behind these stores appear willing to sell merchandise for candidates on both sides of the same race. That raises serious questions about what shoppers are being led to believe. I have no problem with an independent business selling political merchandise. But I do have a problem when a website gives people the impression they're supporting an official campaign without making clear who's actually taking their money. And here's something else worth remembering. The FBI is already warning about election scams involving merchandise that never arrives and fake donation requests. Meanwhile, AI makes it easier than ever to create a convincing website. I wouldn't judge a store by its design or the word "official" in its address. I'd go straight to the organization I want to support and use the links it provides. The same advice applies when you're shopping online or responding to an unexpected request for money. A few extra moments of checking can make a difference. Have you ever purchased something from a website you thought was official, only to discover later that it wasn't connected to the company or organization you wanted to support? Should websites that falsely claim official affiliations face tougher consequences? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com. articles.title: 175 Democrats demand Trump admin stop Ilhan Omar investigation, warn it could hurt her re-election bid
articles.summary: Rep. Pramila Jayapal led 175 House Democrats in accusing DHS and DOJ of weaponizing the federal investigation into Ilhan Omar's immigration history.
articles.body: Nearly 200 House Democrats are moving to shield Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., from further investigation after federal investigators raided her Washington, D.C., home earlier this month. Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., led 175 members of the House Democratic Caucus in a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Attorney General Todd Blanche, criticizing the probe into Omar's immigration history as a partisan attack and accusing them of trying to sway her bid for another term in Congress. "Congresswoman Omar is seeking reelection in Minnesota’s 5th congressional district in just one week. News of the search warrant, whether properly predicated or not, could affect voters’ decisions, which is exactly why federal law enforcement should not engage in such conduct when voters are casting their ballots. This type of interference strips Minnesotans of their right to a free and fair election guaranteed to them under the Constitution," the letter said. "We stand with Congresswoman Omar and condemn the weaponization of law enforcement against her. You have already disgraced the offices you hold, and we demand you refrain from taking any further actions that could affect the outcome of the upcoming election." DEMOCRATS' FURY OVER ILHAN OMAR RAID DRAWS STINGING GOP REMINDER ABOUT RAID FROM THE PAST: ‘SET THE PRECEDENT’ Omar, D-Minn., is under federal investigation over allegations she or her father lied about her birth year on immigration paperwork to obtain her citizenship when her family fled Somalia in the late 1990s. If she was 17 when her father obtained citizenship, as previously thought, she would have automatically qualified along with him. If she was 18 or older, which federal officials now suspect, she would have had to make her own application. FEDERAL AGENTS RAID ILHAN OMAR’S DC HOME AMID IMMIGRATION FRAUD INVESTIGATION Her fellow House Democrats recounted the allegations in their letter, saying, "Your probe into the congresswoman reportedly concerns her late father’s filing of immigration paperwork after she fled Somalia’s civil war at age eight, making her a U.S. citizen at age seventeen." But they argued it does not justify "a pre-dawn raid on her home for paperwork her father filed when she was a minor." DEMOCRATS HAVE ‘DIRTY HANDS’ OVER COMPLAINTS ABOUT OMAR RAID WEEKS BEFORE ELECTION, EX-PROSECUTOR SAYS Federal agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant on Omar's home on Oct. 12, seizing multiple phones and notebooks, among other items. "This weaponization of law enforcement to harass a sitting Member of Congress 22 days before an election is unprecedented and unacceptable," Democrats' letter said. "DOJ has long followed a policy not to take investigative steps relating to a candidate this close to an election if delaying the action will not jeopardize a criminal investigation, a policy which Attorney General Blanche has previously invoked as far back as nine months before an election." ILHAN OMAR BELIEVES TRUMP RAID ON HOME WAS MEANT TO 'INTIMIDATE AND SCARE PEOPLE' FROM VOTING They argued the probe was "driven by a pre-determined political outcome rather than an objective pursuit of justice." Omar has dismissed the probe as a political hit job against one of Trump's loudest critics. Others, however, like House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., have called for Omar to be jailed and deported if the accusations are proven true. articles.title: CBI asked 100 questions in 4.5 hours, most were repetitions; agencies under political pressure: Rajbir Ghuman
articles.summary: CBI questioned Punjab CM Mann’s OSD Rajbir Ghuman for 4.5 hours, he claims 100 repeated questions show political pressure; to appear again Oct 31.
articles.body: Chandigarh: Rajbir Singh Ghuman, officer on special duty (OSD) to chief minister Bhagwant Mann, again appeared before the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Tuesday and said that during the four-and-a-half-hour questioning, he was asked nearly 100 questions, which reflected the “political pressure” on central agencies to target the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) govt in Punjab.Interacting with the media after returning from the questioning, Ghuman said most questions were repetitions of those asked earlier and questioned the timing of the investigative action as elections approached, asserting that attempts to malign CM Mann and his office would not succeed.Ghuman questioned the purpose of the prolonged questioning, stating that most questions had already been asked during previous interactions. While acknowledging that officers were performing their duties, he asked who was exerting pressure on the officers and the investigative agencies.Drawing a parallel with West Bengal, Ghuman said that a similar pattern was being followed in Punjab; Ghuman questioned why the CBI and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) had remained inactive for four years if there was evidence of wrongdoing, and why action was intensifying as elections approached.Ghuman said that he would continue to cooperate with the investigative agencies whenever summoned and confirmed that he would appear before the CBI again on Oct 31.“Investigative agencies were created to protect the Constitution, but today their purpose appears to have changed. The aim is to defame CM Mann and his office through me, but this will not succeed,” he said. Referring to ED raids at govt offices, Ghuman alleged that files are being seized as part of a politically motivated exercise aimed at targeting the Punjab govt.Legal notice to MajithiaSlamming SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia, Rajbir Singh Ghuman alleged that Majithia repeatedly attempted to drag his name into controversies involving drugs, mining and other matters, but would not succeed. “People already know whose name was associated with the drug issue and that Bikram Singh Majithia will not be able to shake off that perception,” he asserted.Ghuman said that he has sent a legal notice to Majithia over repeated attempts to link his name to unrelated matters. In a retort to Majithia, Ghuman challenged the Akali leader to answer questions about his reported stay in the United States. “Did anyone ask Majithia why he ran away to the US and where he stayed there?
